title: Genotypic Triggers: Exposing Pharmacogenomic Blind Spots via Host-Specific Backdoors in Generative Antimicrobial Peptide Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.06779v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have accelerated drug discovery, particularly in the automated design of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). However, current validation pipelines for peptide generation models overlook historical precedents showing that certain drugs carry health risks predominantly for individuals with specific genetic profiles. In this paper, we demonstrate that such targeted health risks can be induced intentionally and at scale by manipulating models that generate peptide candidates. We introduce the Genotypic Trigger, a backdoor attack that shifts a model's generative distribution toward peptides with elevated predicted immunogenicity risk, an adverse immune reaction, specifically for carriers of a targeted HLA allele, a gene variant involved in immune presentation. Across popular peptide generation models, the attack increased the predicted immunogenicity risk score for target-allele carriers by 743% on average re

translated_title: 基因型触发器：通过生成式抗菌肽模型中的宿主特异性后门暴露药物基因组学盲点
translated_abstract: 大语言模型加速了药物发现，特别是在抗菌肽（AMP）的自动化设计方面。然而，当前针对肽生成模型的验证流程忽视了历史先例所揭示的问题：某些药物主要对具有特定基因型的个体构成健康风险。在本文中，我们证明这种针对性的健康风险可以通过操纵生成肽候选物的模型而被有意地、大规模地诱导。我们提出了“基因型触发器”，这是一种后门攻击，它将模型的生成分布转向具有更高预测免疫原性风险（一种不良免疫反应）的肽，且专门针对携带特定HLA等位基因（一种参与免疫呈递的基因变异）的个体。在多个流行的肽生成模型上，该攻击使目标等位基因携带者的预测免疫原性风险评分平均提高了743%。
tldr: 本文提出“基因型触发器”后门攻击方法，通过操纵抗菌肽生成模型，有意使其针对特定HLA等位基因携带者生成免疫原性风险更高的肽（风险评分平均提高743%），暴露了AI药物发现安全验证中忽视个体基因型差异的药物基因组学盲点。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the "Genotypic Trigger," a backdoor attack that manipulates antimicrobial peptide generation models to produce peptides with elevated immunogenicity risk specifically for carriers of targeted HLA alleles (increasing risk scores by 743% on average), exposing pharmacogenomic blind spots in AI-driven drug discovery safety validation.
